summary: Executed Nest Services v2 backend regression (26 pytest tests) and critical frontend smoke via Playwright. Backend: 25/26 passing (96%). Frontend: all key flows (home walkthrough, admin login/dashboard, tenant portal, explore filters, WhatsApp CTA, INR pricing, light ivory theme) verified via Playwright.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout never triggers behind the k8s ingress. `request.client.host` returns the ingress-pod IP (10.227.3.197 / 10.227.3.198 round-robin) instead of the real client IP, so the identifier (`ip:email`) fragments across pods and the count never reaches 5. Verified: 7 consecutive failed logins for the same email all returned 401; DB shows two rows for the same email keyed by different upstream IPs (count=5 and count=2). Fix: derive client IP from `X-Forwarded-For` (first value) or `X-Real-IP` before falling back to `request.client.host`, and key on email only (or email + normalized IP).

rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout RCA: In routers/auth_router.py, the identifier is constructed as `f"{request.client.host}:{email}"`. Behind Kubernetes ingress+service, `request.client.host` is the internal upstream address (10.227.3.197/198), which the ingress balances round-robin across requests from the same external client. Consecutive fails for the same email therefore create N separate `login_attempts` rows (one per upstream IP), none of which ever reach count>=5. Mitigation: read the first hop of `X-Forwarded-For` (or `X-Real-IP`) and use that as the IP component; additionally consider an email-only counter as a secondary guard so the lockout still works when the client IP header is missing.
